_note: Festival and season calendar. Festival dates move every year with the lunar calendar: dates are approximate, to be verified by the owner, and need adding for each new year. 'recurring' events use month-day and repeat every year. regions empty means everywhere in India.

events.name: Christmas and New Year
events.tip: Party season: enjoy the special meals, keep normal portions on the other days and keep walking.

events.name: Sankranti, Pongal, Lohri and Bihu
events.tip: Harvest festival sweets are rich in jaggery and ghee. Have a small piece, not the whole plate.

events.name: Summer heat
events.tip: Hot days: walk or train early morning or after sunset, drink water through the day and have buttermilk, curd and fruit.

events.name: Monsoon
events.tip: Rainy days: swap the outdoor walk for indoor marching, stairs or a home workout, and go easy on fried monsoon snacks.

events.name: Ramadan
events.tip: If you fast: train lightly after iftar, eat protein and slow carbs at sehri, and drink plenty of water between iftar and sehri.

events.name: Holi
events.tip: Holi: enjoy the gujiya and thandai, then get back to your normal plate the next day.

events.name: Chaitra Navratri
events.tip: If you fast: pick roasted makhana, fruit, curd and kuttu or samak dishes over fried vrat snacks, and keep workouts light.

events.name: Navratri and Durga Puja
events.tip: Festival nights: if you fast, choose fruit, curd, makhana and kuttu or samak dishes; garba and pandal walks count as activity.

events.name: Diwali week
events.tip: Diwali week: pick two sweets you love most, skip the rest, and keep your daily walk going.
